semantic_correction.stem: A sexually active adult asks how to reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Which teaching best reflects current CDC guidance?

options.A: Use condoms correctly every time, obtain risk-appropriate STI testing, discuss results with partners, and receive recommended HPV or hepatitis B vaccines.
options.B: Skip testing when neither partner has symptoms, use condoms mainly with new partners, and rely on symptoms to identify infection.
options.C: Use condoms as the sole prevention strategy because correct use completely prevents infections spread through genital skin-to-skin contact.
options.D: Rely on HPV and hepatitis B vaccination instead of testing or barrier protection because vaccination prevents the major sexually transmitted infections.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC prevention guidance recommends a combination of strategies rather than a single measure: use condoms correctly every time, obtain STI testing appropriate to age and sexual risk, communicate with partners and health care providers, and receive vaccines such as HPV and hepatitis B when recommended. CDC notes that most STIs can have no signs or symptoms, so symptom absence does not establish that infection is absent. Because STIs can also spread through genital skin-to-skin contact, condoms reduce risk but do not make all STI transmission impossible. Therefore option A is the most complete and accurate teaching.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach layered STI risk reduction using correct condom use, risk-appropriate testing and communication, and indicated vaccination while correcting misconceptions about asymptomatic infection and complete condom protection.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests layered risk reduction and asymptomatic-infection awareness without overstating condom or vaccine protection.

option_audit.A: Correct. Each element is directly supported by current CDC STI prevention and testing guidance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Many STIs are asymptomatic, and testing should be based on risk rather than symptoms alone.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Condoms reduce risk but cannot fully prevent infections transmitted through uncovered skin-to-skin contact.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. HPV and hepatitis B vaccines prevent specific infections but do not replace other STI prevention and testing strategies.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone combines the CDC-supported prevention layers without a false claim of complete protection.
cueing_check: All four options are multi-part STI-prevention strategies of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
